NONE: › a special thin stick waved by a person who is performing magic tricks

example: The fairy godmother waved her magic wand over the cabbages and they turned into horses.
那位神仙教母將魔杖朝那些捲心菜上揮了兩下，把它們變成了馬。

I or T: B2 [ I or T ] to walk around slowly in a relaxed way or without any clear purpose or direction

I: › [ I ] to start talking about a different subject from the one you were originally discussing
C2 [ I ] If your mind or your thoughts wander, you stop thinking about the subject that you should be giving your attention to and start thinking about other matters.
› [ I ] If you say that an old person's mind is beginning to wander, you mean that they are starting to get very confused because of their age.
（因年老而）神志恍惚，精神錯亂

example: We spent the morning wandering around the old part of the city.
我們整個上午都在老城區閒逛。
She was found several hours later, wandering the streets, lost.
幾個小時後她被找到了，正在街上徘徊，迷路了。
He was here a minute ago but he's wandered off somewhere.
他剛才還在這裡，現在已經閒逛到別的甚麼地方去了。
We've wandered off/from the point somewhat.
我們有點離題了。
Halfway through the meeting my mind started to wander.
會開到一半時我就開始心不在焉了。
Her mind is beginning to wander and she doesn't always know who I am.
她的神志開始恍惚，有時認不出我是誰。

NONE: › time spent travelling around or going from one place or country to another

example: After all her wanderings she had come back home to stay.
經過了諸多漂泊之後，她回到家安定下來。
UK humorous If you see Alan in/on your wanderings, will you tell him he's wanted in the office?
如果你閒逛時見到艾倫，能不能告訴他辦公室裡有人找他？

NONE: › the wish to travel far away and to many different places

example: In July wanderlust takes over the whole nation.
七月全國都是一派旅遊熱的景象。

NONE: › to become weaker in strength or influence
› formal The moon wanes when it gradually appears less and less round, after the full moon.
› becoming less strong, powerful, popular, etc.

example: By the late 70s the band's popularity was beginning to wane.
上世紀70年代末，這個樂團的人氣開始下滑。
There are signs that support for the group is on the wane.
有跡象表明該組織的支持率正日益下降。

NONE: › to succeed in getting or doing something by persuading someone or by being clever in some way

example: I'll be so jealous if you manage to wangle an invitation to his house.
假如你能設法弄到一張去他家的請柬，我會非常嫉妒的。
He's only been here two months and already he's managed to wangle his way into the biggest property company in the capital.
他到這裡才兩個月就已混進首都最大的地產公司了。
If I can think of some excuse to wangle my way out of going tonight I will do!
如果我能找個藉口今晚不去的話，那我一定不會去！

NONE: › a very stupid or unpleasant person, usually a man
笨蛋；無用的男人；卑賤的男人
› very stupid or very poor quality

example: Dave's got some wanky notion that you're only respectable if you own a piece of property.
戴夫有一些愚蠢的想法。他認為除非你有房產，否則你就不會受到尊重。

NONE: › short form of "want to" or "want a"

example: [ + infinitive without to ] Do you wanna go now?
你想現在就走嗎?

NONE: › a person who is trying to become famous, usually unsuccessfully

example: The bar is frequented by wannabe actresses and film directors.
這家酒吧經常有夢想成名的女演員和電影導演光顧。

T: A1 to wish for a particular thing or plan of action. "Want" is not used in polite requests
想要，希望（英國英語中禮貌的請求不用 want）
› to wish or need someone to be present

NONE: › to want to start or stop being involved in something
› used in giving advice to mean that someone should do something

example: I want some chocolate.
我想要些巧克力。
She wants a meeting with you.
她想跟你見面。
He's everything you'd ever want in a man - bright, funny and attractive.
他具備你理想中男人的所有特質——聰明、風趣而又有魅力。
[ + to infinitive ] What do you want to eat?
你想吃甚麼？
[ + obj + to infinitive ] Do you want me to take you to the airport?
你要我送你去機場嗎？
[ + obj + past participle ] This package - do you want it sent today?
這個包裹——你想今天寄出嗎？
[ + obj + adj ] Do you want this pie hot?
這塊餡餅你想要熱一下嗎？
[ + obj + -ing verb ] I don't want you coming in at two a.m., waking me up.
我可不希望你淩晨兩點來，吵得我睡不著覺。
You wait - by next year she'll be wanting a bigger house!
你等著瞧——明年她就會想要一棟更大的房子了！
Am I wanted at the meeting tomorrow?
明天的會議要我參加嗎？
He is wanted by the police (= they are searching for him).
警方正在通緝他。
I want out of the whole venture before it's too late.
我想在還來得及的時候退出整個經營計劃。
Do you think this soup wants a bit of salt?
你覺得這湯裡要不要加點鹽？
[ + -ing verb ] The wine is in the fridge - it just wants cooling for a couple of minutes.
葡萄酒在冰箱裡——只需要冰鎮幾分鐘。
If you ask me that child wants a good slap!
依我說，那孩子就欠狠狠搧一巴掌！
She wants to tell him now, before it's too late.
趁還來得及，她應該現在就告訴他。
You don't want to put too much pepper in.
你不應該放太多胡椒。
For want of anything better to do I watched television for a while.
由於沒有甚麼更好的事情可做，我就看了一會兒電視。
If we fail it won't be for want of trying (= we have tried even if we fail).
即使我們失敗了，我們也曾努力過。
He appeared tired and in want of a shave.
他顯得很疲憊，鬍子也需要刮了。
Our wants are few.
我們所需要的很少。

NONE: › used by sports journalists to refer to a football player who publicly says that they want to leave their current club
（體育記者用來形容）公開表示想離開所屬俱樂部的足球運動員
› wished for and loved by other people
› being searched for by the police because of a crime

example: She was a much wanted baby.

他是個通緝犯。
